**Analyzing Diagonals of Cyan**

I'm currently focusing on the diagonals originating from the cyan cell at (4, 2). The negative-negative diagonal has yielded a candidate at (3, 1) with a value of 4, distance 1. The positive-negative direction seems unpromising, as all values encountered along the diagonal are 0. I'm moving on to explore the final diagonal.


**Refining Target Component**

I've been refining the target component based on the diagonal connections.  The earlier identified potential candidates at (3,1) and (5,1) are indeed part of the same connected component, color 4. Now, I'm analyzing the 4-neighbors of the target cells: (3, 1) and (4, 1), to determine how to wrap the target with cyan correctly and identify cells to be modified. I'm taking the cyan (4, 2) and target (4, 1) into account.

I've been meticulously double-checking the element counts in each row. I found a critical error in row 6 of my output: I added an element inadvertently. The input row 6 was 13 elements, yet my output row had 14. I identified I made an error when converting the 0 in the 3rd column to an 8.
